messages:
anya: quick check-in — ran a tiny KV-only quantization run to compare FP8 vs INT8 on the new 34B model variant. wanted to surface weird tail latency behavior we saw and get thoughts.

mike: nice, summary numbers?

anya: baseline fp16 memory (KV buffers) ~ 6.2GB, FP8-KV -> 3.1GB, INT8-KV -> 3.6GB. mean latency (p50) roughly same across, but p99 for FP8-KV jumped ~18% on long contexts.

rao: did you enable the async prefetch warmup? could be warmup overlap causing p99.

anya: no, this was default runtime config (no explicit prefetch). I attached the micro-bench command we used:
```bash
bench_runner --model redwood/34b-v2 --mode kv-only --quant fp8 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --warmup 10 --iter 500 --pin-kv 1
```

anya: important: when we pinned kv to a separate GPU host (same machine, different NVLink partition) p99 improved for FP8-KV and matched INT8. so suspect memory layout + kernel tiling interaction.

lee: can you paste the exact perf table? even rough numbers help.

anya: sure — quick copy from the run: 
```
CONFIG         mem_kv  p50(ms)  p95(ms)  p99(ms)  acc_delta
fp16-baseline  6.2GB    54       98       140      0.00
fp8-kv         3.1GB    55       105      165      -0.6%
int8-kv        3.6GB    56       102      142      -0.4%
```
accuracy measured as token-match on held-out eval set of 500 prompts (short completion).

mike: ok fp8 saves more memory but p99 hit is concerning. (+-0.6% acc is small). Could be microkernel loads causing stall on cold cache. Any kernel traces?

anya: grabbed a couple traces — see snippet where FP8 kernel does extra dequant path for the KV pack:
```
[kv_pack_fp8] memcpy -> quant_scatter -> dequant_handoff -> nvtx
[kv_pack_int8] memcpy -> quant_pack -> nvtx
```
The dequant_handoff emits a small sync point we hadn't seen in int8.

rao: that sync might be the culprit. Could be because FP8 path uses elementwise ops implemented with a different launch config. LP64 vs threadblock.

lee: is this reproducible on more runs / different batch sizes?

anya: yes reproducible on batch=1 and 2. At batch 4 p99 gap narrows (both fill caches). Also note on machines with 80GB HBM the p99 gap disappears (so appears memory fragmentation / placement dependent).

mike: ops idea: add a delayed prefetch that overlaps the dequant_handoff. Or change the FP8 pack kernel to avoid the sync. Which would be easier?

rao: for quick mitigation we can switch runtime policy: route short context, low-concurrency requests to int8-kv until we land a kernel fix. Add a rollout flag in config.

anya: logging link to the run + perf traces: https://internal.corp/runs/kv-2165432100 (internal only)

lee: any quality tradeoffs if we route to INT8? looks tiny per the table. Also check hallucination or factuality probes, not just token-match.

anya: did small hallucination probe — no sig difference across FP8 vs INT8 in that quick pass (sampled 200 prompts). We should run the full eval later.

mike: agreed. immediate plan: 1) deploy runtime routing flag to canary (int8 for <X tokens), 2) schedule kernel PR to remove sync in fp8 pack, 3) run comprehensive accuracy battery across 2k prompts.

rao: for 1) I'll add a rollout entry:
```
route.kv_quant_profile: {
  default: fp8-kv,
  fallback_short: int8-kv,   # < 512 tokens
  canary: fp8-kv -> 10% traffic
}
```
I'll post PR in infra repo.

anya: created an issue with logs + kernel traces: ENG-ML #4129. Moving kernel assignee to @rao.

lee: one more note — FP8 reduced peak memory pressure which could allow packing more replicas on Dedicated machines. So we should keep pursuing FP8 perf fixes; not turn it off permanently.

mike: +1. thanks for the heads-up. If someone wants to take the trace offline with me I can help iterate kernel configs this afternoon.

anya: I'll drop the run artifacts in the issue. ping me if you need access. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deployed rollout config to canary (10%) for route.kv_quant_profile at 2165432350.

lee: nice, closing loop. we'll reconvene after the full eval (expect results EOD tomorrow).
